notes: Page 1 of a 10-K is a cover page, and it contains BOTH:
(a) a form-style address block -- 'California / 94-2404110 / One Apple
out in two columns of labelled fields. This is NOT a data table.
(b) a genuine 3-column table, 'Securities registered pursuant to
Section 12(b) of the Act', labelled below.
The extractor currently merges (a) into (b) and emits one 14x4 grid. That
is an OVER-MERGE, not a pure false positive: refusing the whole page would
lose a real table, and accepting it as-is ships the cover block as data.
This label exists because the alternative was to invent a rejection
threshold. Measured on the labelled set, neither candidate signal separates
this page from real tables: sparsest-column fill is 21% here but 27% on
Shell p3 and 0% on Apple p30, and column alignment is not all-MIXED. Any
cutoff between 21% and 27% would be fitted to three documents and would
fail on the held-out set. Labelling it makes the failure measurable so a
fix can be judged rather than guessed at.
